sites.name: Quang Trung Museum and Tay Son Tam Kiet Shrine
sites.event: A place preserving artifacts of the Tay Son uprising and the three brothers Nguyen Nhac, Nguyen Hue, and Nguyen Lu; built on the very foundation of their old house, associated with a laterite water well and a giant tamarind tree over 300 years old.

sites.name: Thap Doi Special National Relic
sites.event: A cluster of two ancient Cham towers built around the late 12th to early 13th century, featuring the unique architectural and artistic style of the Champa Kingdom with intricately carved reliefs.

sites.name: Eo Gio Tourist Area
sites.event: A pristine natural landscape with a strait embraced by rocky mountains, famous as one of the most beautiful spots to watch the sunrise in Vietnam.

sites.name: Ky Co Beach
sites.event: A pristine beach with a white sand strip hugging the coastline and clear water with two distinct shades of blue, often referred to as the 'Maldives of Vietnam'.

sites.name: Duong Long Towers Special National Relic
sites.event: The tallest surviving cluster of three brick Cham towers in Southeast Asia, symbolizing the pinnacle of Cham brick and stone architectural sculpture.

sites.name: Heaven and Earth Altar Relic Area (Kinh Thien Dai)
sites.event: The place where the three Tay Son brothers set up an altar to worship Heaven and Earth, received the seal and sword, and prayed before raising troops to establish the Tay Son Dynasty.

sites.name: Ham Ho Eco-tourism Area
sites.event: A scenic natural landscape featuring a majestic river stretch and granite rocks on the riverbed; it was once a strategic military base for the Tay Son insurgent army and Mai Xuan Thuong's insurgent army.

sites.name: Banh It Towers (Silver Tower)
sites.event: A cluster of four Cham towers located on a hill, which is one of the largest ancient tower complexes and bears a strong architectural transition from the My Son A1 style to the Binh Dinh style.

sites.name: Tomb of Poet Han Mac Tu and Ghenh Rang - Tien Sa
sites.event: The resting place of the talented but ill-fated poet Han Mac Tu, located within the Ghenh Rang scenic complex featuring the unique Queen's Beach.

sites.name: Thi Nai Lagoon
sites.event: The largest saltwater lagoon in Binh Dinh Province, featuring a diverse mangrove ecosystem; it was once a fierce naval battlefield in history between the Tay Son and Nguyen Anh forces.

place.commune: Phuoc Thuan Commune, Phuoc Son Commune

sites.name: Thap Thap Di Da Pagoda
sites.event: The oldest ancestral pagoda of the Lam Te Zen sect in Central Vietnam, built on the ruins of 10 collapsed Cham towers in the late 17th century.

sites.name: Emperor Citadel Historical Relic (Do Ban Citadel)
sites.event: The last capital of the Champa Kingdom (Do Ban Citadel), which was later rebuilt by Nguyen Nhac as the headquarters and capital of the Tay Son Dynasty.

sites.name: Canh Tien Tower
sites.event: A solitary Cham tower located right in the center of the Emperor Citadel, featuring elegant architecture with curved roof corners resembling flying fairy wings.

sites.name: Binh Lam Tower
sites.event: A unique Cham tower built right in the plains rather than on hills or mountains, featuring an architectural style transitioning from the 10th to the 11th century.

sites.name: Lo Dieu Numberless Pier Relic
sites.event: The site marking the event of the first numberless ship docking in the waters of Binh Dinh, transporting weapons and supplies to the soldiers and people of Zone V during the resistance war against the US.

sites.name: Nui Ba Historical Relic Area
sites.event: A solid revolutionary base of the soldiers and people of Binh Dinh during the two resistance wars; a mountain complex featuring the largest sitting Buddha statue in Southeast Asia at Linh Phong Pagoda (Ong Nui Pagoda).

sites.name: Cu Lao Xanh Island (Nhon Chau Island)
sites.event: An outpost island with pristine, fresh beauty and an ancient lighthouse built during the French colonial period.

sites.name: Lang Song Church (Lang Song Minor Seminary)
sites.event: One of the first cradles of printing and disseminating the Vietnamese Romanized script (Chu Quoc Ngu) through mass publications in Vietnam; featuring ancient European-style Gothic architecture.

sites.name: Phuong Mai Sand Dunes
sites.event: One of the tallest and most beautiful sand dunes in Central Vietnam, famous for its vast, pristine sandy slopes that change shape with the direction of the wind.

sites.name: Temple of Cultural Celebrity Dao Tan
sites.event: A place to honor and worship Dao Tan - the patron saint of Vietnamese Tuong (classical drama) art, and a great cultural figure of the Nguyen Dynasty.

sites.name: Nguyen Sinh Sac Memorial Site at Binh Khe District Office
sites.event: The site marking the time when Uncle Ho's father served as the district magistrate of Binh Khe, and the location of the historic farewell between the father and son before Nguyen Tat Thanh went south to find a way to save the country.
